questions.why: The big -ir family inserts -iss- in the plural: finissons, finissez, finissent. Singular is finis, finis, finit.
-re verbs take -s, -s, nothing, -ons, -ez, -ent. The il form of vendre is bare vend, with no ending at all.

questions.q: Which of these vous forms does NOT end in -ez?
questions.why: Only three verbs in the language break the -ez pattern: vous êtes, vous faites, vous dites.
Nous faisons is the one verb where -ai- is said as a flat uh sound, so it rhymes with fe-zon and not with fait.
An -er verb in -ger keeps the e before -ons so the g stays soft: mangeons, nageons, voyageons. Compare -cer verbs: nous commençons.
The cedilla keeps the c soft before o. Without it, commencons would be read with a hard k.

questions.q: Which pair is right for préférer?
questions.why: The accent flips to è only where the ending is silent (je, tu, il, ils). Nous and vous have a pronounced ending, so préférons keeps the é.
e_er verbs take a grave accent in the silent-ending forms: j'achète, tu achètes, ils achètent, but nous achetons.

questions.q: Which is the correct present tense of partir for « il » ?
questions.why: Partir belongs to the smaller -ir group that drops the consonant in the singular: pars, pars, part, then partons, partez, partent.
Venir follows the classic irregular silhouette: viens/viens/vient and viennent share one stem, venons/venez another.

questions.q: Build the sentence: She can't come.
questions.why: Pouvoir is conjugated and carries the negation; the second verb stays in the infinitive: elle ne peut pas venir.

questions.q: Translate, using the tense French requires: « I have lived here for three years. » J'habite ici ___ trois ans.
questions.why: Depuis takes the present, because you still live there. Using a past tense here is one of the most persistent English-speaker errors.
The present covers habits as well as the moment: nous mangeons à midi means we eat at noon, every day.

questions.q: Give the six present-tense endings of a regular -er verb, and say which four sound identical.
a: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent. Parle, parles, parle and parlent are all pronounced the same; only parlons and parlez differ.
questions.why: The written endings matter enormously and the spoken ones barely exist, which is why -er verbs are easy to say and easy to misspell.

questions.q: Say this out loud: we do / we make.
questions.why: Faisons is the one place in the language where -ai- is said as a flat uh sound: fe-zon, not fay-zon.
On takes the il form in every tense, so faire gives fait. On fait, never on faisons, even though the sentence means we.
